tagline: A farm village kept rural between two cities.
intro: In Albuquerque NM 448 goes by Coors Road. Across the Sandoval County line it becomes Corrales Road and runs 6.7 miles through a village heavily wooded with cottonwoods on the west side of the Rio Grande, with Albuquerque on one hand and Rio Rancho on the other.

Corrales means corrals. Pueblo farmers worked this ground before the Spanish came, and the ditches still carry river water out to the fields and pastures, while many homes draw their own water from wells.

moments.title: San Ysidro Church
moments.text: A one-story adobe church on Church Road, raised in 1868 for Saint Isidore, the patron of farmers, and given its towers in 1929.

moments.title: Corrales Bosque
moments.text: On the village's eastern edge, 400 acres of cottonwood forest follow the river for ten miles, used by more than 180 kinds of migrating and nesting birds.
